solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S061-01.notes: The blank must name what the observers wrongly believed: records that only the person who tied them could read. 'However' sets this against a consistent system any trained reader could decode, so the answer is 'idiosyncratic' (personal, not shared). A fails: the khipus really are numerical, so 'numerical' cannot be the mistaken dismissal, and it does not explain why only the maker could read them. B means the opposite of the dismissal. D (decorative) does not fit 'records that only the person who tied them could interpret'.

S061-02.notes: The text moves from the first assumption (exposure) to an arrowhead that tore an artery, so the conclusion is that a wound, not the cold alone, most likely killed him. B: no storm is mentioned. C: a torn artery points to a wound received while he was alive, and nothing suggests the arrowhead entered after death. D: why he was crossing the mountains is not supported.

S061-03.notes: The text runs: the paintings survived; visitors' breath brought algae and fungi; the cave was closed and a replica was built. That is popularity endangering a site and a response. A: the text argues nothing about reopening. B: it does not describe the animals. C: no other cave art is mentioned.

S061-04.notes: Text 2 objects that the clearing test judges a body by its surroundings rather than its own nature, and says shape, geology and internal processes are what matter. A: they dispute that the test is a fair one, so they would not simply agree with it. C: they never say Pluto cleared its orbit. D: they would not call every body that orbits the Sun a planet; that goes too far.

S061-05.notes: '...reproduces even the smallest features of the original: the cracks in the rock, the bulges in the walls, and the exact shades...' is an independent clause followed by a colon that introduces the list. Correct. B: a semicolon needs an independent clause after it, and a list is not one. C: 'including:' puts a colon straight after a word that already introduces the list, which is an error. D: with no punctuation, 'the original the cracks in the rock' runs the noun into the list.

S061-06.notes: 'By the time officials closed... in 1963' marks an action finished before a past event, so it needs the past perfect 'had spread'. A (present) and B (present perfect) clash with the past time frame. D (future) is illogical.

S061-07.notes: People still calling Pluto a planet contrasts with the reclassification, so 'Nevertheless' fits. A: it is not a consequence. B: it is not an example. C: it is not a similar point.

flags.note: Shares content with S061-02, and the note 'Researchers now think the wound most likely caused his death' gives away S061-02's answer if both items appear in the same set or module. Do not place them together.

S061-08.notes: Only B shows both the first view (exposure) and the later view (wound), so it alone shows a change in understanding. A and D only report the discovery. C states the X-ray finding but not that the earlier view was revised.

S061-09.notes: The text sets the old method (walking between drawers) against the new one (an online search in seconds), so 'By contrast' fits. A: the new method is not an example of the old. C: the two are opposed, not similar. D: online search is not a result of walking between drawers.

S061-10.notes: A states the limitation: there was no negative, so each image could not be reproduced. B, C and D give only historical or technical facts and name no limitation.
